notes:
CycloneDX is a Bill of Materials (BOM) standard. Originally created within OWASP; now developed jointly by the OWASP Foundation and Ecma International Technical Committee 54 (TC54) and published as ECMA-424 (2025-12-10). The canonical project home is cyclonedx.org. CycloneDX supports SBOM, SaaSBOM, HBOM (hardware), ML-BOM (machine learning), OBOM (operations), MBOM (manufacturing), CBOM (cryptography), VDR and VEX.

ML-BOM is a capability of the one BOM schema rather than a separate schema file: it is expressed through the machine-learning-model and data component types plus the modelCard and componentData objects. Those elements are addressable here as #mlbom/... subpaths mirroring the schema's own field paths. Item-level nodes resolve against 1.7 documentation and record since_version 1.5 — the release that introduced model cards. CycloneDX 1.4 and earlier have no ML-BOM support.

data.description: A lightweight Bill of Materials (BOM) standard designed for application security contexts and supply chain component analysis. Supports SBOM, SaaSBOM, HBOM, ML-BOM, OBOM, MBOM, CBOM, and VDR (Vulnerability Disclosure Report).
data.notes:
Multiple format encodings (JSON, XML, Protocol Buffers). Widely used in modern SBOM tooling — Trivy, Syft, Anchore, Dependency-Track all produce or consume CycloneDX. Companion/alternative to SPDX. A data format; the value-add is in the tools that produce/consume CycloneDX, not in standalone judgement guidance — placed under reference.

Standardised as ECMA-424 under Ecma TC54. Version 1.7 (2025-10-21) is current. Schema files for each version are listed in urls below and follow the stable pattern https://cyclonedx.org/schema/bom-<version>.{schema.json,xsd,proto}.

children.description: ML-BOM — the CycloneDX machine learning bill of materials capability

data.description: Machine Learning Bill of Materials. Provides model and dataset transparency for security, privacy, safety and ethical considerations by describing models, the datasets they were trained and evaluated on, and their dependencies.
data.notes: ML-BOM is not a separate schema file. It is the subset of the BOM schema comprising the machine-learning-model and data component types, the modelCard object attached to a machine-learning-model component, and the componentData object attached to a data component. Model card support is derived from the TensorFlow Model Card Toolkit and portions of VerifyML, both Apache-2.0.

children.description: Component type that makes a CycloneDX BOM an ML-BOM

data.description: Specifies the type of component. For software components, classify as application if no more specific appropriate classification is available or cannot be determined for the component.
data.notes: These are two values of the components[].type enumeration. A machine-learning-model component SHOULD carry a modelCard; a data component SHOULD carry componentData. Neither object may be attached to any other component type.

known_values.mlbom/component/machine-learning-model: A model based on training data that can make predictions or decisions without being explicitly programmed to do so.
known_values.mlbom/component/data: A collection of discrete values that convey information.

data.description: A model card describes the intended uses of a machine learning model and potential limitations, including biases and ethical considerations. Model cards typically contain the training parameters, which datasets were used to train the model, performance metrics, and other relevant data useful for ML transparency. This object SHOULD be specified for any component of type `machine-learning-model` and must not be specified for other component types.
data.notes: Anchor paths on the CycloneDX documentation page are generated by walking $refs, and modelCard is fully expanded at exactly one place in that walk — under metadata.tools. That is why resolution URLs carry the metadata_tools_oneOf_i0_components_items_ prefix even though the field being described is components[].modelCard. It is the real link target; a tidier-looking anchor would resolve to nothing.

data.description: A field of modelParameters, quantitativeAnalysis or considerations.
data.notes: considerations/* is the block most often cited in AI governance work — intended users, use cases, technical limitations, performance tradeoffs, ethical risks, environmental impact and fairness assessments. Anchor paths on the CycloneDX documentation page are generated by walking $refs, and modelCard is fully expanded at exactly one place in that walk — under metadata.tools. That is why resolution URLs carry the metadata_tools_oneOf_i0_components_items_ prefix even though the field being described is components[].modelCard. It is the real link target; a tidier-looking anchor would resolve to nothing.

known_values.mlbom/modelCard/modelParameters/approach: The overall approach to learning used by the model for problem solving.
known_values.mlbom/modelCard/modelParameters/task: Directly influences the input and/or output. Examples include classification, regression, clustering, etc.
known_values.mlbom/modelCard/modelParameters/architec: The model architecture family such as transformer network, convolutional neural network, residual neural network, LSTM neural network, etc.
known_values.mlbom/modelCard/modelParameters/modelArc: The specific architecture of the model such as GPT-1, ResNet-50, YOLOv3, etc.
known_values.mlbom/modelCard/modelParameters/datasets: The datasets used to train and evaluate the model.
known_values.mlbom/modelCard/modelParameters/inputs: The input format(s) of the model
known_values.mlbom/modelCard/modelParameters/outputs: The output format(s) from the model
known_values.mlbom/modelCard/quantitativeAnalysis/per: The model performance metrics being reported. Examples may include accuracy, F1 score, precision, top-3 error rates, MSC, etc.
known_values.mlbom/modelCard/quantitativeAnalysis/gra: A collection of graphics that represent various measurements.
known_values.mlbom/modelCard/considerations/users: Who are the intended users of the model?
known_values.mlbom/modelCard/considerations/useCases: What are the intended use cases of the model?
known_values.mlbom/modelCard/considerations/technical: What are the known technical limitations of the model? E.g. What kind(s) of data should the model be expected not to perform well on? What are the factors that might degrade model performance?
known_values.mlbom/modelCard/considerations/performan: What are the known tradeoffs in accuracy/performance of the model?
known_values.mlbom/modelCard/considerations/ethicalCo: What are the ethical risks involved in the application of this model?
known_values.mlbom/modelCard/considerations/environme: What are the various environmental impacts the corresponding machine learning model has exhibited across its lifecycle?
known_values.mlbom/modelCard/considerations/fairnessA: How does the model affect groups at risk of being systematically disadvantaged? What are the harms and benefits to the various affected groups?

known_values.mlbom/componentData/type: The general theme or subject matter of the data being specified.
known_values.mlbom/componentData/contents: The contents or references to the contents of the data being described.
known_values.mlbom/componentData/classification: Data classification tags data according to its type, sensitivity, and value if altered, stolen, or destroyed.
known_values.mlbom/componentData/sensitiveData: A description of any sensitive data in a dataset.
known_values.mlbom/componentData/graphics: A collection of graphics that represent various measurements.
known_values.mlbom/componentData/description: A description of the dataset. Can describe size of dataset, whether it's used for source code, training, testing, or validation, etc.
known_values.mlbom/componentData/governance: Data governance captures information regarding data ownership, stewardship, and custodianship, providing insights into the individuals or entities responsible for managing, overseeing, and safeguarding the data throughout its lifecycle.
